A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. V3's Extended Data A-C can be matched to material incorporated into v4's main text; no essential reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original fine-tuning and prompting experiments measuring racial FPR gaps, plus accuracy and gap-span analyses in Extended Data B-C.

after.justification: V4 reports original fine-tuning and prompting results in Figures 1-4, with accuracy statistics and gap-span rankings in Tables 2-4.

M1.justification: The fine-tuning, zero-shot, 9-shot and zero-shot CoT procedures are retained. Template construction, label mappings, LoRA adaptation and prediction extraction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use Amazon, NS-Prompts and Regard for the same six racial-group sentiment evaluations, SST5 for fine-tuning, and SST5/SemEval for demonstrations. No dataset, task, population or language coverage is added.

E2.justification: The prompting comparison drops LLaMA-7B and adds Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B, retaining OPT-6.7B and Llama-2-7B (v3 Table B3(b); v4 Table 2). The fine-tuning comparison set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new model evaluations introduce an 8B prompting configuration, whereas v3 prompted only 6.7B/7B models. Temperature 0.8, demonstration selection, token limits, inference batch sizes and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3's Extended Data B quantifies how often White-group gaps define span extremes: 58% for negative-sentiment FPR and 100% for positive-sentiment FPR. V4 retains the qualitative observation and ranking table but omits these supplementary summaries and the discussion comparing span distributions.

E5.justification: Both retain five-run means, 95% confidence intervals, accuracy standard deviations, prompting seeds 2024-2028, and selection of five from fifteen runs for smaller fine-tuned models. New result rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds Llama-3/Mistral prompting accuracies and FPR-gap results and removes LLaMA-7B results. The best listed configuration changes from Llama-2-7B/SemEval 9-shot (0.654) to Llama-3-8B/SST5 9-shot (0.716), involving different configurations. OPT-6.7B/SemEval accuracy changes from 0.481 to 0.482. Fine-tuning results and gap-span rankings retain their values; the extreme-gap percentages are omitted.

T1.justification: The group-relative metric dM(X), positive/negative FPR definitions and maximum-minus-minimum gap-span definition are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and closing discussion retain the central claim that explicit demographic templates can produce misleading bias measurements, with markedness-related mismatch proposed as the explanation. No new central contribution or established causal result is claimed.

C2.justification: V4 removes the closing discussion's explanation that multimodal models may overcome some reporting bias while still retaining markedness effects. The main markedness interpretation, suggested remedies and need for future validation remain.

D1.justification: V3 points to 'supplementary information 1' for source code; v4 supplies a specific GitHub repository address. V4 also documents identifiers for the newly prompted models. Hyperparameter-search details are relocated with equivalent values.

R1.justification: Four cited works are removed: Abid et al. (2021), Norlund et al. (2021), Alper et al. (2023), and C. Zhang et al. (2022) on visual commonsense. The broader research positioning is retained; most other reference changes concern formatting.

P1.justification: V4 moves related work and methodology ahead of the results and integrates the former Extended Data sections into the main narrative. Paragraph condensation and language editing throughout accompany this substantial reorganization.

P2.justification: The single-column document becomes two-column. V3's pipeline schematic is removed, and result plots are redrawn with revised proportions, markers, legends and captions. Extended-data tables are relocated, and the two-part accuracy table becomes separate Tables 2 and 3.

improvement.justification: Prompting results for Llama-3 and Mistral strengthen the check that anomalies persist without fine-tuning on models already included in the fine-tuning experiments. The specific code pointer and methods-before-results organization improve usability. These limited gains outweigh the lost pipeline schematic, supplementary summaries and multimodal qualification. The markedness explanation remains unconfirmed.
